# std/http.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from std/http.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

HTTP/1.1 over std/net.bastio, for programs on the hosted
target: a client that fetches a page, and the building blocks of a server
(accept a request, answer it). Every message is sent with
`Connection: close`, so a body ends where the connection does and no
chunked transfer is needed. A parser for a request head that is safe
against hostile input is examples/http/http.bastio, and `http_accept`
uses it: a request whose head it rejects is answered with 400 and never
reaches the caller.

What is proved: no read or write is out of bounds, and every buffer is
freed. Not proved: that a peer speaks HTTP, that what is read stays within
the limit given (the socket call's result is opaque to the prover), or
that a response is complete.

`import "std/http.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md), [core/bytes.bastio](core-bytes.md), [std/net.bastio](std-net.md), `examples/http/http.bastio`, [core/text.bastio](core-text.md), [core/num.bastio](core-num.md).

| Function | |
| --- | --- |
| [`http_get_request`](#http_get_request) | The request for `GET path` from `host`. |
| [`http_response`](#http_response) | A response with status `status`, reason phrase `reason`, content type `ctype` and body `body`. |
| [`http_body_start`](#http_body_start) | Where the body starts. |
| [`http_status`](#http_status) | The status code of a response (0 if the status line is not `HTTP/1.x NNN`). |
| [`http_read_head`](#http_read_head) | Reads from `sock` until the bytes read hold a whole head (an empty line), or fails if the peer closes first or the head is longer than `limit`. |
| [`http_read_all`](#http_read_all) | Reads from `sock` until the peer closes it, or fails if more than `limit` bytes arrive. |
| [`http_read_response`](#http_read_response) | Reads one response from `sock` and returns it whole, status line and headers included, without waiting for the peer to close. |
| [`http_get`](#http_get) | Sends `GET path` to `ip`:`port` (the `Host` header says `host`) and returns the whole response, at most `limit` bytes, status line and headers included. |
| [`http_accept`](#http_accept) | Accepts a connection on the listening socket `sock` and reads its request head (at most `limit` bytes). |
| [`http_read_request`](#http_read_request) | Reads the next request head (at most `limit` bytes) from the connection `conn`, which `http_accept` or an earlier answer left open. |
| [`http_req_target`](#http_req_target) | The request target of `r` (the path and query of `GET /a?b HTTP/1.1`), or empty if the request line has none. |
| [`http_req_is`](#http_req_is) | Is the request method the literal `m`? |
| [`http_req_body`](#http_req_body) | Reads the body of the request `r` from its connection and returns it, decoded. |
| [`http_req_keeps`](#http_req_keeps) | May the connection of `r` carry another request once it is answered? Yes for HTTP/1.1 without `Connection. |
| [`http_answer`](#http_answer) | Answers `r` with a response made from `status`, `reason`, `ctype` and `body`, and frees the request. |
| [`http_reply`](#http_reply) | Sends `resp` (build it with `http_response`) on the request's connection, closes the connection and frees the request. |
| [`http_close`](#http_close) | Closes the request's connection and frees the request. |

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Types and constants

### `HttpReq`

```bastio
struct HttpReq { conn: u64, head: Bytes, req: Req }
```

A request that has been read: the connection it came on, the bytes read
so far (the head, and possibly the start of a body) and where the strict
parser found the method, the target and the fields in them.

## Functions

### `http_get_request`

```bastio
fn http_get_request(host: Str, path: Str) -> Bytes
```

The request for `GET path` from `host`.

Example:

```bastio
let r = http_get_request("example.org", "/index.html");
let want = bfrom("GET /index.html HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: example.org\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n");
let ok = bytes_eq(r, want);
bfree(r);
bfree(want);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `http_response`

```bastio
fn http_response(status: u64, reason: Str, ctype: Str, body: &Bytes) -> Bytes
```

A response with status `status`, reason phrase `reason`, content type
`ctype` and body `body`.

Example:

```bastio
let body = bfrom("hi");
let r = http_response(200, "OK", "text/plain", body);
let want = bfrom("HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: text/plain\r\nContent-Length: 2\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\nhi");
let ok = bytes_eq(r, want);
bfree(r);
bfree(want);
bfree(body);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `http_body_start`

```bastio
fn http_body_start(m: &Bytes) -> Option[u64]
```

Where the body starts: just past the empty line that ends the head.

Example:

```bastio
let m = bfrom("HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nA: b\r\n\r\nbody");
let mut ok = false;
match http_body_start(m) {
  Option::Some(i) => { ok = i == 25; },
  Option::None => {},
}
bfree(m);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `http_status`

```bastio
fn http_status(m: &Bytes) -> u64
```

The status code of a response (0 if the status line is not
`HTTP/1.x NNN`).

Example:

```bastio
let m = bfrom("HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found\r\n\r\n");
let s = http_status(m);
bfree(m);
if s != 404 { return 1; }
```

### `http_read_head`

```bastio
fn http_read_head(h: &Host, sock: u64, limit: u64) -> Option[Bytes]
```

Reads from `sock` until the bytes read hold a whole head (an empty line),
or fails if the peer closes first or the head is longer than `limit`. The
result may end with the first bytes of a body.

Example:

```bastio
// The head ends at the empty line; a peer that stops sooner is an error.
let lo = net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1);
let mut bad = 1;
match net_listen(host, lo, 0) {
  Option::Some(s) => {
    let p = net_port(host, s);
    match net_connect(host, lo, p) {
      Option::Some(c) => {
        match net_accept(host, s) {
          Option::Some(a) => {
            let part = bfrom("GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\n");
            let sent = net_send_all(host, c, part);
            bfree(part);
            net_close(host, c);
            match http_read_head(host, a, 4096) {
              Option::Some(m) => { bfree(m); },
              Option::None => { if sent { bad = 0; } },
            }
            net_close(host, a);
          },
          Option::None => { net_close(host, c); },
        }
      },
      Option::None => {},
    }
    net_close(host, s);
  },
  Option::None => {},
}
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `http_read_all`

```bastio
fn http_read_all(h: &Host, sock: u64, limit: u64) -> Option[Bytes]
```

Reads from `sock` until the peer closes it, or fails if more than `limit`
bytes arrive.

Example:

```bastio
// Everything the peer sends, up to its close.
let lo = net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1);
let mut bad = 1;
match net_listen(host, lo, 0) {
  Option::Some(s) => {
    let p = net_port(host, s);
    match net_connect(host, lo, p) {
      Option::Some(c) => {
        match net_accept(host, s) {
          Option::Some(a) => {
            let msg = bfrom("abcdef");
            let sent = net_send_all(host, a, msg);
            bfree(msg);
            net_close(host, a);
            match http_read_all(host, c, 100) {
              Option::Some(m) => { if sent && bytes_eq_str(m, "abcdef") { bad = 0; } bfree(m); },
              Option::None => {},
            }
          },
          Option::None => {},
        }
        net_close(host, c);
      },
      Option::None => {},
    }
    net_close(host, s);
  },
  Option::None => {},
}
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `http_read_response`

```bastio
fn http_read_response(h: &Host, sock: u64, limit: u64) -> Option[Bytes]
```

Reads one response from `sock` and returns it whole, status line and
headers included, without waiting for the peer to close: the head, then
the `Content-Length` bytes it names. A response with no `Content-Length`
is read to the peer's close, as `http_read_all` does it; a chunked one
is read to its last chunk and returned with the body decoded after the
head, which is left as it came. A head that is not a valid response head,
a message longer than `limit` and a peer that closes early give `None`.

Example:

```bastio
// A response on a connection that stays open.
let lo = net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1);
let mut bad = 1;
match net_listen(host, lo, 0) {
  Option::Some(s) => {
    let p = net_port(host, s);
    match net_connect(host, lo, p) {
      Option::Some(c) => {
        match net_accept(host, s) {
          Option::Some(a) => {
            let body = bfrom("hello");
            let resp = http_response_with(200, "OK", "text/plain", body, true);
            let sent = net_send_all(host, a, resp);
            bfree(resp);
            bfree(body);
            // The connection is still open: this returns at once.
            match http_read_response(host, c, 4096) {
              Option::Some(m) => {
                if sent && http_status(m) == 200 { bad = 0; }
                bfree(m);
              },
              Option::None => {},
            }
            // A chunked response on the same connection comes back decoded.
            let ch = bfrom("HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\n\r\n3\r\nhel\r\n2\r\nlo\r\n0\r\n\r\n");
            let sent2 = net_send_all(host, a, ch);
            bfree(ch);
            match http_read_response(host, c, 4096) {
              Option::Some(m) => {
                match http_body_start(m) {
                  Option::Some(at) => {
                    if !sent2 || at > blen(m) || !bytes_span_eq_str(m, at, blen(m), "hello") { bad = 1; }
                  },
                  Option::None => { bad = 1; },
                }
                bfree(m);
              },
              Option::None => { bad = 1; },
            }
            net_close(host, a);
          },
          Option::None => {},
        }
        net_close(host, c);
      },
      Option::None => {},
    }
    net_close(host, s);
  },
  Option::None => {},
}
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `http_get`

```bastio
fn http_get(h: &Host, ip: u64, port: u64, host: Str, path: Str, limit: u64) -> Option[Bytes]
```

Sends `GET path` to `ip`:`port` (the `Host` header says `host`) and
returns the whole response, at most `limit` bytes, status line and
headers included. Check it with `http_status`; the body starts at
`http_body_start`.

Example:

```bastio
// Nothing listens on port 1, so there is no response.
let mut none = true;
match http_get(host, net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1), 1, "localhost", "/", 65536) {
  Option::Some(r) => { bfree(r); none = false; },
  Option::None => {},
}
if !none { return 1; }
```

### `http_accept`

```bastio
fn http_accept(h: &Host, sock: u64, limit: u64) -> Option[HttpReq]
```

Accepts a connection on the listening socket `sock` and reads its request
head (at most `limit` bytes). A connection that sends no whole head in
that much is closed and gives `None`.

Example:

```bastio
// The request goes through a loopback connection made in the example.
let lo = net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1);
let mut bad = 1;
match net_listen(host, lo, 0) {
  Option::Some(s) => {
    let p = net_port(host, s);
    match net_connect(host, lo, p) {
      Option::Some(c) => {
        let req = http_get_request("localhost", "/hello");
        let sent = net_send_all(host, c, req);
        bfree(req);
        match http_accept(host, s, 4096) {
          Option::Some(r) => {
            let t = http_req_target(r);
            if sent && bytes_eq_str(t, "/hello") { bad = 0; }
            bfree(t);
            http_close(host, r);
          },
          Option::None => {},
        }
        net_close(host, c);
      },
      Option::None => {},
    }
    net_close(host, s);
  },
  Option::None => {},
}
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `http_read_request`

```bastio
fn http_read_request(h: &Host, c: u64, limit: u64) -> Option[HttpReq]
```

Reads the next request head (at most `limit` bytes) from the connection
`conn`, which `http_accept` or an earlier answer left open. A peer that
closes it, or sends no whole head, or a head the strict parser rejects
(answered with 400) gives `None`, and the connection is closed.

Example:

```bastio
// Two requests, one after the other, on one connection.
let lo = net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1);
let mut bad = 1;
match net_listen(host, lo, 0) {
  Option::Some(s) => {
    let p = net_port(host, s);
    match net_connect(host, lo, p) {
      Option::Some(c) => {
        match net_accept(host, s) {
          Option::Some(a) => {
            let r1 = http_get_request("x", "/one");
            let sent = net_send_all(host, c, r1);
            bfree(r1);
            match http_read_request(host, a, 4096) {
              Option::Some(q) => {
                let t = http_req_target(q);
                if sent && bytes_eq_str(t, "/one") { bad = 0; }
                bfree(t);
                http_close(host, q);
              },
              Option::None => {},
            }
          },
          Option::None => {},
        }
        net_close(host, c);
      },
      Option::None => {},
    }
    net_close(host, s);
  },
  Option::None => {},
}
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `http_req_target`

```bastio
fn http_req_target(r: &HttpReq) -> Bytes
```

The request target of `r` (the path and query of `GET /a?b HTTP/1.1`), or
empty if the request line has none.

### `http_req_is`

```bastio
fn http_req_is(r: &HttpReq, m: Str) -> bool
```

Is the request method the literal `m`?

Example:

```bastio
let lo = net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1);
let mut bad = 1;
match net_listen(host, lo, 0) {
  Option::Some(s) => {
    let p = net_port(host, s);
    match net_connect(host, lo, p) {
      Option::Some(c) => {
        let req = http_get_request("localhost", "/");
        let sent = net_send_all(host, c, req);
        bfree(req);
        match http_accept(host, s, 4096) {
          Option::Some(r) => {
            if sent && http_req_is(r, "GET") && !http_req_is(r, "POST") { bad = 0; }
            http_close(host, r);
          },
          Option::None => {},
        }
        net_close(host, c);
      },
      Option::None => {},
    }
    net_close(host, s);
  },
  Option::None => {},
}
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `http_req_body`

```bastio
fn http_req_body(h: &Host, r: &HttpReq, limit: u64) -> Option[Bytes]
```

Reads the body of the request `r` from its connection and returns it,
decoded: `Content-Length` bytes, or the data of a chunked body without the
framing, or nothing if the request has neither field. Gives `None` if the
framing is ambiguous or invalid (a repeated `Content-Length`, both
fields, a transfer coding other than a lone `chunked`: see `http_body`),
if the body is longer than `limit` bytes, or if the peer closes or fails
before the body is whole. The request stays open for the answer.

Example:

```bastio
// A POST with a Content-Length body, then one with a chunked body.
let lo = net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1);
let mut bad = 1;
match net_listen(host, lo, 0) {
  Option::Some(s) => {
    let p = net_port(host, s);
    let mut n = 0;
    while n < 2 {
      match net_connect(host, lo, p) {
        Option::Some(c) => {
          let mut req = bfrom("POST /x HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\nContent-Length: 5\r\n\r\nhello");
          if n == 1 {
            bfree(req);
            req = bfrom("POST /x HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\n\r\n3\r\nhel\r\n2\r\nlo\r\n0\r\n\r\n");
          }
          let sent = net_send_all(host, c, req);
          bfree(req);
          match http_accept(host, s, 4096) {
            Option::Some(r) => {
              match http_req_body(host, r, 4096) {
                Option::Some(b) => {
                  if sent && bytes_eq_str(b, "hello") { bad = 0; }
                  bfree(b);
                },
                Option::None => { bad = 1; },
              }
              http_close(host, r);
            },
            Option::None => { bad = 1; },
          }
          net_close(host, c);
        },
        Option::None => { bad = 1; },
      }
      n = n + 1;
    }
    net_close(host, s);
  },
  Option::None => {},
}
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `http_req_keeps`

```bastio
fn http_req_keeps(r: &HttpReq) -> bool
```

May the connection of `r` carry another request once it is answered? Yes
for HTTP/1.1 without `Connection: close`, with no body, and with nothing
read past the head (a client that sent the next request early gets the
connection closed after the answer instead).

Example:

```bastio
// HTTP/1.1 keeps; asking to close, or HTTP/1.0, does not.
let lo = net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1);
let mut bad = 1;
match net_listen(host, lo, 0) {
  Option::Some(s) => {
    let p = net_port(host, s);
    bad = 0;
    let mut n = 0;
    while n < 3 {
      match net_connect(host, lo, p) {
        Option::Some(c) => {
          let mut req = bfrom("GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\n\r\n");
          if n == 1 {
            bfree(req);
            req = bfrom("GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\nConnection: Keep-Alive, CLOSE\r\n\r\n");
          }
          if n == 2 {
            bfree(req);
            req = bfrom("GET / HTTP/1.0\r\nHost: x\r\n\r\n");
          }
          let sent = net_send_all(host, c, req);
          bfree(req);
          match http_accept(host, s, 4096) {
            Option::Some(r) => {
              if !sent || http_req_keeps(r) != (n == 0) { bad = 1; }
              http_close(host, r);
            },
            Option::None => { bad = 1; },
          }
          net_close(host, c);
        },
        Option::None => { bad = 1; },
      }
      n = n + 1;
    }
    net_close(host, s);
  },
  Option::None => {},
}
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `http_answer`

```bastio
fn http_answer(h: &Host, r: HttpReq, status: u64, reason: Str, ctype: Str, body: &Bytes) -> Option[u64]
```

Answers `r` with a response made from `status`, `reason`, `ctype` and
`body`, and frees the request. The response says `Connection:
keep-alive` and the connection is returned, still open, when
`http_req_keeps` allows it; otherwise it says `Connection: close` and the
connection is closed (also when the answer could not be sent) and the
result is `None`. The next request on a returned connection is read with
`http_read_request`.

Example:

```bastio
// Two requests on one connection: the first is answered with keep-alive,
// the second asks to close.
let lo = net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1);
let mut bad = 1;
match net_listen(host, lo, 0) {
  Option::Some(s) => {
    let p = net_port(host, s);
    match net_connect(host, lo, p) {
      Option::Some(c) => {
        match net_accept(host, s) {
          Option::Some(a) => {
            let r1 = bfrom("GET /one HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\n\r\n");
            let sent1 = net_send_all(host, c, r1);
            bfree(r1);
            let body = bfrom("ok\n");
            let mut kept = 0;
            match http_read_request(host, a, 4096) {
              Option::Some(q) => {
                match http_answer(host, q, 200, "OK", "text/plain", body) {
                  Option::Some(k) => { kept = k; },
                  Option::None => {},
                }
              },
              Option::None => {},
            }
            let r2 = http_get_request("x", "/two");
            let sent2 = net_send_all(host, c, r2);
            bfree(r2);
            if sent1 && sent2 && kept != 0 {
              match http_read_request(host, kept, 4096) {
                Option::Some(q) => {
                  // Connection: close in the request, so no keep-alive.
                  match http_answer(host, q, 200, "OK", "text/plain", body) {
                    Option::Some(k) => { net_close(host, k); },
                    Option::None => { bad = 0; },
                  }
                },
                Option::None => {},
              }
            }
            bfree(body);
          },
          Option::None => {},
        }
        net_close(host, c);
      },
      Option::None => {},
    }
    net_close(host, s);
  },
  Option::None => {},
}
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `http_reply`

```bastio
fn http_reply(h: &Host, r: HttpReq, resp: &Bytes) -> bool
```

Sends `resp` (build it with `http_response`) on the request's connection,
closes the connection and frees the request.

Example:

```bastio
// A whole exchange in one process: the client's request is already in the
// socket's buffer when the server reads it, and the answer is when the
// client does.
let lo = net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1);
let mut bad = 1;
match net_listen(host, lo, 0) {
  Option::Some(s) => {
    let p = net_port(host, s);
    match net_connect(host, lo, p) {
      Option::Some(c) => {
        let req = http_get_request("localhost", "/hi");
        let sent = net_send_all(host, c, req);
        bfree(req);
        match http_accept(host, s, 4096) {
          Option::Some(r) => {
            let body = bfrom("hello");
            let resp = http_response(200, "OK", "text/plain", body);
            let ok = http_reply(host, r, resp);
            bfree(resp);
            bfree(body);
            match http_read_all(host, c, 4096) {
              Option::Some(m) => {
                let mut at = 0;
                match http_body_start(m) { Option::Some(i) => { at = i; }, Option::None => {} }
                if sent && ok && http_status(m) == 200 && at <= blen(m) && blen(m) - at == 5 { bad = 0; }
                bfree(m);
              },
              Option::None => {},
            }
          },
          Option::None => {},
        }
        net_close(host, c);
      },
      Option::None => {},
    }
    net_close(host, s);
  },
  Option::None => {},
}
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

```bastio
fn http_close(h: &Host, r: HttpReq)
```

Closes the request's connection and frees the request.

Example:


## Internals

### `http_response_with`

```bastio
fn http_response_with(status: u64, reason: Str, ctype: Str, body: &Bytes, keep: bool) -> Bytes
```

Internal: `http_response` with `Connection: keep-alive` when `keep`.

### `http_read_chunked`

```bastio
fn http_read_chunked(h: &Host, sock: u64, first: &Bytes, limit: u64) -> Option[Bytes]
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> blen(result.Some) <= limit && limit <= 1073741824
```

Internal: the decoded body of a chunked message. `first` holds the bytes
that followed the head when it was read; the rest comes from `sock` until
the last chunk. The decoded body is at most `limit` bytes.

### `http_is_connection`

```bastio
fn http_is_connection(s: &Bytes, a: u64, b: u64) -> bool
  requires a <= b && b <= blen(s)
```

Internal: does `s[a..b)` spell "connection", ignoring case?

### `http_has_close`
